gitCommit.subject: History tells grace decisions in its own words; the console names a paid end's message by its outcome
gitCommit.body:
History tells grace decisions in its own words; the console names a paid end's message by its outcome

- The subscription history knew neither 0099 event kind: a grace started and a period that ended with none left both
  read "Change recorded", followed by the server's English note, in French and Arabic alike. grace_started and
  grace_unavailable now have their own words in EN/FR/AR and are told from catalogue sentences with the period end the
  server recorded (periodEndAfter), in the business's zone and isolated in Arabic, as the trial's events are; an event
  without a period end says so without a date. The server's note is no longer shown for them.
- The console's message log and a business's messages named both paid-end messages "paid period ended". With the
  row's variant they now say "paid period ended — grace started" or "— no grace left" (EN/FR/AR). The portal's
  summary is unchanged: its status panel already states the grace outcome.

Found on the real-API screenshots of the rehearsal. Tests: every kind has words in each language (the two added);
grace told in French and Arabic with the zone's date and never the server's note; both variant names in the console;
the source rule extended to the grace kinds. Gates: typecheck; Vitest 33 files, 534/534; the three production builds
refused without their inputs; full, public and portal previews with 0 broken links and the bundle audits passing;
Playwright full 138/138, public 148/148, portal 34/34.
